title: The enemy study becomes a canyon lane: a file closing on MÖRK, the ram premium, the splat and the hull bogging down
context: The first cut of labs.html#swarm orbited a grid of bodies on a turntable. The owner's note after looking at it was that a grid teaches nothing: put them in a long file in a game-like canyon with walls, heading at the tank, crashing into a moving tank, with the animation, the sound, the RAM bonus and the slight slowdown on impact — make it feel more real.
outcome: The lab is a lane now: a 300-long canyon with walls and a lip, a file of bodies closing from the far end, and the hull ploughing them. The rules are the game's, imported rather than re-typed — RAM_PREMIUM, STREAK_CAP and STREAK_STEP from domain/economy, rammable and bounty from ENEMY_SPEC, the splat from units.makeDotBurst, the death cues from the shared audio bank. A rammable belt goes under the treads for bounty x premium x a capped streak; a solid core stops the hull instead and breaks the chain, because letting the tank plough a drifter would teach the wrong thing about the belt ladder the lab exists to study. Every impact costs the hull speed it earns back at 1.9/s, so a dense file genuinely bogs it down. Controls: body, dot cloud or jelly, in-the-lane count to 1200, density, file width, tank charging/weaving/parked, chase/side/top/free views, walls and sound. The cost readout stays, because look and cost are the two questions asked at once. Three faults were found by screenshotting rather than by any test: the bodies were scaled near the hull's own size and read as trees beside it, fixed by driving scale from ENEMY_SPEC.size against the hull radius; the HUD sat under the chrome menu button main.js injects top-left, moved right; and the file was a field rather than a column, fixed with a narrower lateral spread, the full lane depth and a charge that sweeps rather than eases down the middle. MÖRK now stands in the lane: the procedural hull builds on the first frame and the real GLB swaps in when preloadMork resolves, so the lane runs immediately rather than waiting on a download. Measured sustained on an M4: 303 kills in 30 s, a chain of 303, 3,198 kg, hull oscillating 0.28 to 0.91, 420 bodies at 1.9 us each.
alternatives: Keep the turntable and add a count slider: rejected by the owner on sight; a crowd reads by how it funnels, not by how it spins.
Wait for MÖRK before showing anything: rejected, a lab that waits on a GLB to draw its first frame is one nobody opens twice; the procedural hull covers the gap.
Let the tank ram everything for a better kill rate: rejected, the rammable/solid split is the read the whole roster is built on.
evidence: scripts/browser-test.mjs case swarm-study now asserts the lane runs: kills climb, a chain forms, ramming pays, the hull slows, a white belt never blocks, and a drifter blocks and is never rammed — plus motion per family and the jelly arriving as triangles.
npm test, npm run check, npm run build, npm run test:browser and node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist all pass.
Screenshots at 1500x940 DPR2 through the headless harness; the scale, HUD and column faults were visible there and in no test.
